articles.title: How Chael Sonnen got caught using PED's #ufc
articles.description: Even Chael Sonnen—the man known for confidence and relentless trash talk—has experienced genuine fear before a fight. In this clip, Chael recalls walking out to face Brian Stann in Houston, Texas, after Stann had knocked out three opponents. As the curtain opened and his music started, Chael says he froze, thinking, “Please don’t.” He describes the pressure of having to put on his fight-night face and make the walk despite the nerves. The conversation then turns to Chael’s suspension and the evolution of UFC drug testing. He discusses out-of-competition testing, admits he was trying to work around the rules, and explains his perspective on performance-enhancing drugs during a commission hearing. It’s an unusually candid look at the fear, pressure, and mindset behind a major UFC fight—and Chael’s own account of the choices that led to his suspension. Watch as Chael Sonnen reflects on the Brian Stann fight, his walkout nerves, and the drug-testing system. #ChaelSonnen #BrianStann #UFC #MMA #UFCHistory #MMAStories #DrugTesting #PerformanceEnhancingDrugs #FightNight

articles.title: Why One UFC Fight Doesn’t Tell the Whole Story #ufc
articles.description: A fight can last 12 seconds—and that still doesn’t tell you everything about a fighter. Chael Sonnen uses Jorge Masvidal’s famous knockout of Ben Askren to make a bigger point about MMA. Did that one moment prove Masvidal was a better fighter or that he had better skills than Askren? Chael argues that fights can turn on a single moment, and fans shouldn’t let one result create an entire narrative about a fighter. His message to wrestlers is even more direct: don’t abandon what made you successful just because people tell you that you need to become more exciting or completely reinvent yourself. Being well-rounded, entertaining, and marketable can help get you into the Octagon. But once you’re there, Chael says the objective becomes much simpler. You just have to win. #ChaelSonnen #UFC #MMA #JorgeMasvidal #BenAskren #Wrestling #MMAAnalysis #UFCHistory #FightStrategy

articles.title: Why Ilia Topuria Lost to Justin Gaethje #ufc
articles.description: Ilia Topuria had Justin Gaethje hurt—but according to Chael Sonnen, one decision may have changed the entire fight. Chael breaks down Sean O’Malley’s take on the matchup, specifically the moment in the second round when Topuria dropped Gaethje with a body shot. O’Malley believes Ilia could have finished the fight if he had simply walked away instead of following Gaethje to the ground. Chael agrees with the bigger point: Topuria’s year away from competition may have been the difference over 25 minutes. Moving countries, changing gyms, disrupting his training schedule, and returning after a long layoff created a difficult set of circumstances for a fighter trying to maintain championship-level performance. Chael also makes the case for just how decorated Topuria already was—an undefeated UFC champion, former No. 1 pound-for-pound fighter, and two-division champion. He argues that the paperwork surrounding the BMF title may have kept Topuria from adding another championship to his résumé. Was the year-long layoff the real reason Ilia Topuria came up short against Justin Gaethje? #ChaelSonnen #IliaTopuria #JustinGaethje #SeanOMalley #UFC #MMA #BMF #UFCLightweight #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Chael Sonnen was always a heel #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen didn’t become “The Bad Guy” overnight. He says he spent nearly a decade trying to get attention for his fights—and repeatedly got shut down. Looking back at his early UFC years in 2005 and 2006, Chael recalls trying to play the heel while calling out Chuck Liddell and mocking his appearance. In one interview with Sherdog reporter Loretta Hunt, he says she stopped the recording because his persona was so different from what she expected. The interview was never published. And that wasn’t the only time. Chael describes how his college wrestling coach intervened during local newspaper interviews, preventing his provocative comments from reaching print. Without today’s social media platforms, those missed opportunities made it difficult to build a public persona or generate interest in his matches. In this clip, Chael explains the years of frustration behind his fight-promotion style—and how people who didn’t understand his approach kept getting in the way. #ChaelSonnen #UFC #MMA #TheBadGuy #ChuckLiddell #Sherdog #TrashTalk #MMAHistory #UFCStories

articles.title: Dana Got Banned. How Far Does Eddie Go?
articles.description: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are finally fighting, fourteen years late, for nothing, and the most interesting man in the whole saga isn't allowed in the building. Eddie Hearn posted the contract verbiage himself: no Zuffa, no TKO, and no Dana White, with Dana named personally so nobody can hide behind an entity. Dana skipped the press conference, reportedly barred by the very contract Hearn put on the internet. Chael watched the presser twice and came away with nothing compelling from either fighter. Turki Alalshikh ran the show with a hot mic the whole time, and Chael still isn't sure who's actually paying for any of it, only that Eddie Hearn never spends his own money. Here's Chael's real take: the fight itself has nothing on it. No belt, no bad blood, both men politely claiming England, fourteen years after anyone asked for it. The only interesting thing about the entire proposition is Hearn versus Dana. And his prediction: this fight scares everybody away. MMA runs 44 weekends a year, and on that night, everyone stays out of the way. articles.title: Josh Hokit’s Secret Weapon Against Ciryl Gane #ufc
articles.description: Josh Hokit doesn’t necessarily need to take Ciryl Gane down to beat him. According to Chael Sonnen, he just needs Gane to believe the takedown is coming. Chael breaks down how Hokit’s wrestling threat could open up striking opportunities against the heavyweight contender. He points to Hokit’s fight with Derrick Lewis, where an explosive early takedown forced Lewis to respect the possibility of another one—and changed the dynamics of the fight. Against Gane, that same threat could make Hokit’s striking more dangerous. Chael also explains how Hokit could use his wrestling to control the fight, grind out rounds, and potentially win a decision. With the November 14 matchup in focus, Chael discusses the different ways Hokit could get the job done, from a knockout to a wrestling-heavy performance. Can Hokit’s wrestling pressure create the opening he needs to finish Ciryl Gane? #ChaelSonnen #JoshHokit #CirylGane #UFC #MMA #Heavyweight #Wrestling #DerrickLewis #UFCAnalysis

articles.title: Chael Sonnen’s Best Trash Talk Talk (Nogueira Brothers) #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen’s infamous Nogueira brothers joke is one of the most memorable moments in MMA trash-talk history—and it nearly cost him his fighting license. Chael recounts the story of claiming that when the Nogueira brothers first arrived in America, one tried to feed a bus a carrot while the other petted it, believing it was a horse. The absurd insult left the interview host struggling to respond, but the controversy didn’t end with the punchline. Chael says the Nevada executive director at the time threatened to pull his license, arguing that children might look up to him. The twist? Chael insists he used no profanity or threats—just a deliberately outrageous story designed to provoke a reaction. In this clip, Chael explains how the bit was planned, why it was so unusual at the time, and how his approach to trash talk pushed the boundaries of MMA promotion. Was this Chael Sonnen’s greatest trash-talk moment? articles.title: The Dana–Hearn Feud Is Driving Headlines #ufc
articles.description: Is the feud between Dana White and Eddie Hearn becoming a bigger story than Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua? Chael Sonnen breaks down the growing tension between the UFC boss and the boxing promoter, questioning whether their public clash is also generating valuable attention for the heavyweight matchup. He suggests that, whether the conflict is orchestrated or completely genuine, the headlines and interview requests surrounding Dana and Eddie may be drawing more attention than the proposed fight itself. Eddie Hearn has argued that Dana White should have no involvement in the event’s press conferences or promotional activities. Dana, meanwhile, has pushed back, questioning who could stop him from being involved. Chael says he’s reluctant to turn against Hearn, recognizing that promoting the fight is his job. But he also points out that the rivalry between the two promoters is capturing significant attention in North America. Is this a genuine feud, a promotional masterclass, or both? #ChaelSonnen #DanaWhite #EddieHearn #TysonFury #AnthonyJoshua #FuryJoshua #Boxing #UFC #MMA #BoxingNews

articles.title: Justin Gaethje Has a Decision to Make #ufc
articles.description: Arman Tsarukyan has been positioned as the UFC’s leading lightweight contender, and Chael Sonnen says there should be no debate about his place in the title picture. Chael points to Arman receiving a contract to fight for the championship and then being named as a backup who could step in on just 24 hours’ notice. He argues that Justin Gaethje’s response to a potential matchup will carry significance, particularly amid discussion of Gaethje’s retirement. Chael compares the situation to Jon Jones’ past reluctance to pursue a fight with Tom Aspinall, while noting an important distinction: Gaethje has expressed willingness to fight whoever the UFC asks him to face, provided the weight is right. Chael sees that willingness as consistent with the expectations placed on a champion. The discussion explores Arman’s contender status, Gaethje’s next move, and the expectations surrounding fighters who say they will take on anyone. #ChaelSonnen #ArmanTsarukyan #JustinGaethje #UFC #MMA #UFCLightweight #JonJones #KhabibNurmagomedov #UFCNews

articles.title: The secret behind Chael Sonnen’s trash talking  #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen didn’t become “The Bad Guy” by accident. He studied what makes a fighter entertaining—and turned it into an art. In this conversation, Chael explains how legendary boxers like Sugar Ray Leonard, Mike Tyson, and Muhammad Ali inspired his understanding of fight promotion. The biggest stars weren’t simply the ones with the best records or the hardest punches. They were the ones who could tell a compelling story and make fans care about what happened next. Chael also breaks down the difference between naturally embracing a heel or face persona and deliberately studying how to build a fight. Drawing on the five W’s—who, what, when, where, and why—he explains why great promotion comes down to great storytelling, not just championships or undefeated records. From professional wrestling’s approach to creating stars to the psychology of fight promotion, this is Chael Sonnen’s philosophy behind the art of the bad guy. Subscribe for more Chael Sonnen interviews, UFC analysis, MMA stories, and insights into the business of combat sports. #ChaelSonnen #UFC #MMA #TheBadGuy #FightPromotion #TrashTalk #UFCHistory #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Gable Steveson Has Already Proven Himself #ufc
articles.description: Does Gable Steveson really not belong in the UFC after a 12-second fight? Chael Sonnen strongly challenges that argument. Chael pushes back against media critics who questioned Steveson’s place in the promotion, pointing out that a brief fight sequence shouldn’t erase his accomplishments—or the fact that he had already won inside the UFC. He compares the criticism to questioning whether Jose Aldo belonged in the sport after his similarly short loss to Conor McGregor. Chael also highlights Steveson’s wrestling background, his ability to recover from setbacks, and the impression he has made so far. He references Joe Rogan’s reported message to Dana White about the impact Steveson could have on the division. The discussion examines what one short fight can—and cannot—prove about a fighter’s potential, and why Chael believes Steveson deserves more opportunity before being written off. #GableSteveson #ChaelSonnen #UFC #MMA #JoeRogan #DanaWhite #Wrestling #UFCHighlights #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Nobody Will Call Him Out
articles.description: Nobody in the UFC will call out Ateba Gautier. Not one guy. And Chael Sonnen knows exactly why. This Saturday at UFC 332 in Salt Lake City, "The Silent Assassin" meets Roman Kopylov, and Chael breaks down why the matchmakers' hardest puzzle just got harder. Gautier has ended nearly everything early, and Chael says he has never personally seen anyone survive a round with him. Kopylov is the perfect test and the perfect warning: a zombie who keeps coming forward no matter how hard you hit him, the guy who always says yes. Chael is confident we finally see Gautier in the second and third rounds, and that changes everything. Then comes the story behind the fighter: poisoned as a boy in his village by a jealous man he trusted, given up for dead by the medicine man, and saved by a religious woman who laid him before a serpent statue, had his brothers hold him down with no anesthesia, and cut the poison out of him. He felt it leave his body. Whatever you believe, you will see Gautier differently after hearing it. Timestamps: [0:00] The hardest guy in the UFC to match up [0:30] Nobody has survived a round with Gautier [0:40] Roman Kopylov: the zombie who never goes away [0:57] Gautier finally sees the second and third round [1:30] Gautier's faith runs deeper than most fighters [1:55] Poisoned as a kid by a jealous villager [2:42] The medicine man gives up on him [3:00] The woman takes him into her house [3:40] The serpent statue [4:09] "Hold him down": no anesthesia, no doctor [4:16] She cuts into him, stitches him up, he lived [4:43] He felt the relief when she cut into him [4:58] He walked home knowing he was okay [5:24] You'll view Gautier differently now Watch more Chael Sonnen breakdowns right here on the channel. #UFC #MMA #AtebaGautier

articles.title: Should Arman Tsarukyan Be Ranked Ahead of Ilia Topuria? #ufc
articles.description: Should Arman Tsarukyan be ranked ahead of Ilia Topuria—or should the former two-division champion get another shot at the UFC title? Chael Sonnen breaks down a complicated lightweight title picture. He argues that Ilia’s recent championship success and pound-for-pound standing make it difficult to dismiss his claim to another opportunity, even after losing the belt. At the same time, Chael believes Arman is the division’s No. 1 contender and discusses a potential matchup with Justin Gaethje. The debate comes down to competing claims: Arman’s position as a leading contender versus Ilia’s championship résumé, including his status as a two-division world champion. Chael explains why a title shot for Ilia wouldn’t necessarily be unreasonable, even if Arman is next in line. Who should get the next lightweight title opportunity? Hear Chael’s analysis of the rankings, contenders, and possible UFC matchups. #ChaelSonnen #ArmanTsarukyan #IliaTopuria #JustinGaethje #UFC #MMA #UFCLightweight #UFCRankings #TitleShot
